content: 1. Capsules containing 200 mg of the drug should be administered orally once daily. Oral solutions containing 240 mg should also be administered orally once daily. 2. For patients with a creatinine clearance (CrCl) of 50 mL/min or greater, the recommended dose is 200 mg of the capsule orally once daily or 240 mg of the oral solution once daily. 3. For patients with a CrCl between 30-49 mL/min, the capsule dose should be reduced to 200 mg orally every 48 hours, while the oral solution dose should be adjusted to 120 mg orally once daily. 4. For patients with a CrCl between 15-29 mL/min, the capsule dose should be further reduced to 200 mg orally every 72 hours, and the oral solution dose should be adjusted to 80 mg orally once daily. 5. For patients with a CrCl less than 15 mL/min, the capsule dose should be 200 mg orally every 96 hours, and the oral solution dose should be 60 mg orally once daily. 6. On the day of hemodialysis, the medication should be administered after the dialysis session. 7. This medication is indicated for the treatment of HIV infection in combination with other antiretroviral agents. 8. Dose adjustments or increased dosing intervals are necessary based on renal function. 9. The combination of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be co-administered with other antiretroviral agents. 10. Co-administration of emtricitabine-containing products with lamivudine-containing products should be avoided due to the increased risk of immune reconstitution syndrome and therapeutic duplication. 11. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) medications may interfere with the manufacturing of certain cell-based therapies, such as atidarsagene autotemcel, betibeglogene autotemcel, elivaldogene autotemcel, and lovotibeglogene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 12. Co-administration of emtricitabine with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase serum concentrations of emtricitabine. Examples include acyclovir, adefovir, ganciclovir, valacyclovir, valganciclovir, and NSAIDs such as ibuprofen, diclofenac, and naproxen. 13. Co-administration of emtricitabine with high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs may result in toxicity. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 14. Drugs like ribavirin and zidovudine increase the risk of lactic acidosis and immune reconstitution syndrome when used with emtricitabine. 15. Orlistat may decrease the absorption of emtricitabine, potentially leading to loss of virological control in HIV-infected patients. HIV RNA levels should be monitored frequently, and orlistat should be discontinued if viral load increases. 16. Ritonavir and nirmatrelvir/ritonavir may increase emtricitabine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 17. Co-administration of emtricitabine with immunosuppressive agents like ublituximab may reduce the efficacy of emtricitabine and increase the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified and closely monitored. 18. Patients receiving emtricitabine with other antiretroviral agents, such as efavirenz, nevirapine, or tipranavir, should be monitored for immune reconstitution syndrome. 19. Co-administration of emtricitabine with drugs like sulindac, piroxicam, or tolmetin may increase toxicity due to reduced renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 20. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period before cell-based therapies to ensure complete elimination of the medications.
